recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Further core changes should be made only under a new Security WG decision if the current Break the Glass examples or policy guidance are redesigned.
issue_request: FHIR-5935 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 Security WG issue requesting that the Break the Glass discussion make clear that the tag/header is not a complete FHIR-defined interoperable process; the approved resolution was to add a note that use depends on an agreed implementation policy and protocol outside FHIR.
initial_application: Commit 1ca8cc96b8a6323b76b0d91ec3eeed92067ab06a, whose message includes #5935, added the requested sentence to source/security-labels.html in 2015.
additional_context: FHIR-14192 later reworked the Break the Glass material and retained the same point as broader guidance that FHIR does not define policy or protocol for such requests. FHIR-53885 then moved the section from Security Labels to the Security page because the examples are security-principles guidance rather than security-labeling guidance.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. source/security.html:450-486 already states that Break the Glass representation methods do not define policy or protocol and lists responsibilities for initiation, authorization/consent/access control, audit representation, and notifying clinicians that Break the Glass is available; source/security-labels.html correctly records that the standalone section moved.

related_jiras.note: Reworked the Break the Glass discussion while preserving the FHIR-5935 policy/protocol caveat as broader implementation guidance.
Moved the Break the Glass section from Security Labels to the Security page, keeping the policy/protocol guidance in the current source location.
